feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
A recent discussion evaluates enhancements to Bitcoin’s transaction signature scheme, particularly focusing on aspects of BIP118 and proposed modifications. The suggestion is made that the `hashSequence` field does not require blanking for eltoo’s functionality, especially since `sighash_single` is employed in scenarios where it becomes relevant. By removing this redundant blanking step, the design could restrict the potential to alter the number of transaction inputs in a NOINPUT context, as `hashSequence` would remain the sole component committing to the set of inputs.
The proposal introduces a `sighash_scriptmask`, which receives a favorable response due to its approach of committing to scripts when feasible. This modification addresses some shortcomings of BIP118 by ensuring stronger commitments within the signature hash. Additionally, there is an endorsement for the mechanism that commits to transaction fees while still providing a `nofee` escape hatch, offering both flexibility and reliability in fee management.
However, concerns are raised regarding the addition of a new opcode intended to mask elements within the sighash. This approach is compared to the earlier introduction of `codeseparator`, suggesting it might represent a similar violation of the protocol’s layering principles. Despite this observation, the issue is considered minor relative to the overall benefits of the proposal.
For further technical detail and collaborative discussion, interested readers may consult the [bitcoin-dev mailing list](https://lists.linuxfoundation.org/mailman/listinfo/bitcoin-dev), where these proposals and their implications are actively debated by contributors.
